Description: Aléxios Komnenos Stratigópoulos holds an immortal place in world history as the liberator who restored Constantinople to the Roman Empire. Elevated to the exalted ranks of Grand Domestic and Caesar, Alexios was a battle-hardened tactician of daring vision and impeccable timing. Learning through local peasant volunteers that the entire Latin garrison and Venetian fleet had departed to assault Daphnousia island, Alexios seized the historic moment with breathtaking audacity. Guiding his infiltrators through a secret culvert near the Pege Gate under cover of night, he opened the city walls, set torch to Venetian commercial quarters, and provoked absolute panic that sent Latin Emperor Baldwin II fleeing without his crown. In a single stroke of military genius, Alexios ended fifty-seven years of Western Crusader occupation, restoring Byzantine sovereignty to the Queen of Cities. At Pelagonia, Alexios demonstrated tactical mastery by springing a coordinated cavalry ambush that routed Latin crusaders. As dawn illuminated the Golden Horn, Alexios stood in gilded mail before Hagia Sophia proclaiming the resurrection of the Roman Empire, moving citizens to tears and sealing his immortal glory.
Motivations: Seize any strategic opportunity to recover Constantinople and erase the humiliation imposed by the Fourth Crusade upon the Roman people.
Break Latin and Epirote resistance at Pelagonia and on the European frontier, clearing the way for imperial restoration.
Lead disciplined frontier raiding troops, defend recovered European lands and honour the Strategopoulos family through military service.
Values: Opportunities are fleeting; a commander must risk life and fortune when decisive action is needed rather than hesitate.
Lead surprise attacks personally, combining strict discipline and care for soldiers with calm, daring and precise judgement.
Serve Rome and Orthodoxy loyally, treating recovery of the capital as a divine calling rather than a means to private reward.
Fears: Informers exposing the tunnel attack on Constantinople, allowing Latin troops to ambush all eight hundred soldiers and ruin the chance of recovery.
A united western counterattack after Constantinople's recovery striking before imperial resources are sufficient and destroying the city again.
SpeechStyle: His voice commands instant obedience, resolute and razor-sharp, inspiring absolute courage in the face of impossible military odds.
